headline: A second bounce day (semis +1.9%) leaves every AI segment still down 8-27% on the month, with a 5.15% 10-year and rising VIX capping the rebound.
regime: AI-bottleneck stocks rose again on the close (semis ETF +1.9%, servers +4.3%, neoclouds +2.9%), but five-day returns are still negative in nearly every hardware segment and the VIX is up 28% in a month to 18.1. The 10-year yield rose to 5.15% and headlines cite oil above $110 on Iran tensions, so the market is still paying for cash flow and software, the only segment up over the month (+4.5%). Demand news is strong (Super Micro's preliminary quarter, Micron's $61.5B guide); the pressure is on financing and valuation, not orders.

theses.title: Power, grid and cooling, not chips, limit the AI build-out
evidence: NextDC's 40% selloff came from power constraints and community opposition (81d7dcc8478c)
Google's 1 GW bring-your-own-capacity deal in PJM shows hyperscalers paying to secure grid capacity (1e6dc66c2306)
Nvidia and Vertiv's 14-day modular AI factory design targets deployment speed, the other half of the constraint (dba2adf82ddc)
theses.change_note: More evidence of the same theme, but grid and power equipment fell 4% over five days (PWR -9%), so no reason to add confidence.

theses.title: AI compute demand still outruns supply
evidence: Super Micro raised fiscal Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B on AI platform demand (6ae19d904b11)
Micron posted a $54.2B quarter and guided to $61.5B (99e1010ac86e)
Super Micro and Nvidia launched a 256-CPU Vera rack for agentic AI (e83799b6a0c6)
theses.change_note: Two more hard supplier numbers beat expectations; +2 because the order book is confirmed by revenue, not by commentary.

theses.title: Debt-funded neoclouds are where the AI cycle breaks first
evidence: CoreWeave bond yields top 15% and a credit expert calls it the canary for AI distress (00ac2b0c193a, e402e9592e49)
Galaxy Digital faces scrutiny over CoreWeave's rising debt at its Helios site (ac158c89587a)
Nebius took a $3.5B financing facility, which funds growth but adds leverage (740a51ba79ec)
The segment is down 26.6% over a month despite +2.9% today
theses.change_note: Bond yields above 15% are the clearest stress reading so far; a one-day bounce does not change it.

theses.title: Memory is priced as if this is the peak of the cycle
evidence: Micron's $61.5B guide and 379% revenue growth sit beside a 4.4x forward P/E (99e1010ac86e)
Analysts upgraded Seagate on hard-drive demand tied to data centres (6cc3bd881946)
The segment is down 21.6% in a month, the second worst after neoclouds
theses.change_note: Fundamentals improved but the stock reaction was negative again (Micron fell Thursday), which is what a market pricing peak margins does. Held at 55.

theses.title: Hyperscaler capex is eating their free cash flow
evidence: Meta reported a nearly $10B hit in Q3 even as revenue outlook was strong, and META fell 5.4% over five days (035c5aafa782)
Oracle is selling stock, adding debt and using customer prepayments to fund its AI push (d7cd1007b7eb)
Microsoft is committing a $700B moat in AI spend through 2030, funded by cash flow (0563b598faef)
theses.change_note: Microsoft shows the funded version and Oracle the strained one; nothing today moves the aggregate view.

theses.title: The AI trade is crowded and rates are high
evidence: The 10-year yield rose to 5.15% and SoftBank's value is poised to halve from its peak on higher borrowing costs (35bbe47a6ae8)
Fidelity's Timmer places the bubble risk in debt, not stock valuations (00ac2b0c193a)
Nasdaq futures fell premarket as AI spending worries resurfaced (d1579c98041e)
theses.change_note: +5: yields are higher, the VIX is up and the premarket reaction to good news was selling.

compute.note: Demand is solid but the group is down 12% on the month and still crowded.

foundry_equipment.note: Down 4.7% over five days and Lam Research led premarket losses on AI spending doubts.

memory_storage.note: Micron at 4.4x forward earnings after a 22% monthly drop; the cycle-peak risk is the price of entry.

networking_optical.note: Down 5.2% in five days; strong growth but no valuation cushion.

servers.note: Super Micro's raise lifted the group, but HPE is -7.8% over five days and margins stay thin.

power_nuclear.note: Prefer cash-generating producers such as NRG; pre-revenue nuclear is down over 60% this year.

grid_electrical.note: Slowest part of the build to expand, but down 4% over five days and Quanta is -9%.

cooling_thermal.note: Vertiv's modular design with Nvidia is a good sign ahead of its earnings next week.

datacenter_neocloud.note: Bond yields above 15% at CoreWeave; avoid until financing clears.

hyperscalers.note: Only segment down on the day (-0.5%); capex still outruns free cash flow.

ai_software.note: Up 4.5% on the month and 4.0% today; momentum, not a bottleneck play.

risks: A 10-year yield at 5.15% and rising compresses valuations across the AI chain.
Oil above $110 in headlines (the tape shows $99) on Iran tensions could feed inflation and keep rates high.
Memory earnings at 4x may be peak-cycle; a pricing turn would cut them fast.
Credit stress at CoreWeave could spread to its suppliers through cancelled orders.
A rising VIX (+28% in a month) signals the market is paying for protection.
watch: Whether Thursday's close holds after futures fell sharply on Meta and Tesla earnings.
Vertiv earnings next week as a read on cooling demand.
CoreWeave bond yields against the 15% level.
The 10-year yield against 5.15% and the VIX against 18.
Western Digital and Seagate earnings for a read on hard-drive pricing.
